newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan firms to invest in Indonesian gas field.
newsitem.headline: Japan firms to invest in Indonesian gas field.

text.p: Teikoku Oil Co Ltd said on Wednesday that a group of 11 Japanese companies have decided to buy a 13 percent stake in a natural gas field in the South China Sea from Indonesian state oil and gas company Pertamina.
The gas field is expected to produce 15 million tonnes of liquified natural gas a year from early in the next decade, a spokesman for Teikoku Oil said.

The Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Wednesday that the consortium of three oil companies -- Teikoku, Indonesia Petroleum Ltd and Japan Petroleum Exploration Co Ltd -- and eight trading houses including Mitsubishi Corp, Mitsui & Co Ltd and Nissho Iwai Corp, will invest 250 billion yen in the two trillion yen natural gas project.
It said the semigovernmental Japan National Oil Corp will also be taking part in the project along with the 11 private-sector firms.
But the Teikoku spokesman did not disclose the total amount of investment.
